why: This is a study-specific named measurement instrument for surveying perceptions of online-course engagement strategies, not a reusable instructional element.
name: 38-item engagement strategies survey instrument
product_description: A 38-item self-report survey developed and used by Martin et al. to measure online higher-education students' perceived benefits of learner-to-learner, learner-to-instructor, and learner-to-content engagement strategies.

why: This is a meta-analysis evidence pool and its empirical findings about PBL, not a reusable instructional element or implementation design.
The set is a narrow image-based instance of selected-response multiple-choice assessment items, so its evidence belongs on the canonical page rather than constituting a new instructional element.
